---
applyTo: "**/*.java"
---

# Backend Coding Standards — Temple Registry

## Package Structure

```
com.templeregistry/
 ├── controller/
 ├── service/
 │    └── impl/
 ├── repository/
 ├── entity/
 ├── dto/
 │    ├── request/
 │    └── response/
 ├── mapper/
 ├── config/
 ├── exception/
 └── util/
```

Never place business logic outside `service/impl/`. Never expose `entity/` objects through API responses.

---

## BaseEntity

- Every entity MUST extend `BaseEntity` (`@MappedSuperclass`). Never create a JPA entity that does not extend it.
- `BaseEntity` carries: `id BIGINT UNSIGNED`, `is_deleted BOOLEAN`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`.
- PK generated by the DB via `AUTO_INCREMENT`. Use `@GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)`. Never generate PKs manually in application code.
- `@NoArgsConstructor` required for JPA instantiation — include it alongside `@Builder` + `@AllArgsConstructor`.
- `createdAt` and `updatedAt` set in `@PrePersist`. `updatedAt` refreshed in `@PreUpdate`.
- `createdBy` and `updatedBy` populated from `SecurityContextHolder` in `@PrePersist` / `@PreUpdate`.
- Define `equals()` and `hashCode()` on entity subclasses using only the `id` field.

---

## Soft Delete

- Every entity must carry `@SQLRestriction("is_deleted = false")` (Hibernate 6.x / Spring Boot 3.x). Do NOT use the deprecated `@Where`.
- Use `@SQLDelete` to intercept JPA `deleteById` and perform a soft-delete `UPDATE` instead of a `DELETE`. The SQL must match the entity's `@Table(name)` exactly.
- Never issue `DELETE FROM` in JPA, JPQL, or native queries unless data-retention policy explicitly requires it.
- Cascade rule: when a parent entity is soft-deleted, all children in the same aggregate must be soft-deleted within the same transaction.

---

## Controllers

- Return type: `ResponseEntity<ApiResponse<T>>` on every method.
- `@Valid` on every `@RequestBody`.
- No business logic. No try-catch. No `@Autowired` — constructor injection only via `@RequiredArgsConstructor`.
- Every endpoint documented with `@Operation` and `@ApiResponse` (Swagger/OpenAPI).

---

## Services

- Every service must have an interface and a separate `*ServiceImpl` class. No bare `@Service` without an interface.
- `@Transactional` on every write method. `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` on every read method.
- `@PreAuthorize` required on every state-modifying method. Reference a constant from `RoleConstants`.
- `@EnableMethodSecurity` must be on the security config class — without it, `@PreAuthorize` is silently ignored.
- Log the action name and entity ID only. Never log the full payload, passwords, tokens, or PII.
- Pagination guard: enforce `Math.min(requestedSize, 100)` before constructing `PageRequest`.

---

## Repositories

- DB access only. No business logic.
- Use `@EntityGraph` or `JOIN FETCH` on every query that loads associations. Never rely on lazy loading inside a loop.
- All single-entity lookups must return `Optional<T>`.
- Index every FK column and every `status` column in the Flyway migration.

---

## DTOs

- Separate request and response DTO classes. Never reuse the same class for both directions.
- Validation annotations (`@NotBlank`, `@Size`, etc.) on request DTOs only.
- Never return or reference entity classes in any API surface.

---

## Mappers

- MapStruct only (`@Mapper(componentModel = "spring")`). No manual field-by-field mapping in services.
- No logic inside mappers — mapping only.
- Use `@Mapping(target = "...", ignore = true)` for fields populated by `BaseEntity` lifecycle hooks (`id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`).

---

## Global Exception Handler

- One `@RestControllerAdvice` class handles all exceptions project-wide. Never add try-catch in controllers or services.
- Must handle at minimum: `EntityNotFoundException` → 404, `MethodArgumentNotValidException` → 400, `Exception` fallback → 500.
- Never expose stack traces in response bodies.
- Log expected domain errors at `WARN`. Log unexpected exceptions at `ERROR`.
- All error responses must conform to the `ApiResponse` error envelope: `{ "success": false, "message": "...", "errorCode": "...", "errors": [] }`.

## ApiResponse Wrapper

- Define a generic `ApiResponse<T>` class with static factory methods: `ApiResponse.success(message, data)`, `ApiResponse.error(message, errorCode)`, `ApiResponse.validationError(message, errors)`.
- Every controller method returns `ResponseEntity<ApiResponse<T>>`. No bare response bodies.

---

## Pagination

- Use `PaginatedResponse<T>` as the `data` payload on all list-endpoint responses.
- `PaginatedResponse<T>` must carry: `content`, `page`, `size`, `totalElements`, `totalPages`, `last`.
- Provide a static `PaginatedResponse.of(Page<T>)` factory method.
- Default page size: 10. Maximum: 100. Enforce the max in the service layer.

---

## Flyway Migrations

- All schema changes via Flyway SQL migrations only. Never use `ddl-auto: update` or `ddl-auto: create` in any environment.
- Location: `src/main/resources/db/migration/`
- Naming: `V{n}__{description}.sql` (e.g., `V1__create_temples_table.sql`)
- Every FK column and every `status` column must have a corresponding `CREATE INDEX` statement in the same migration file.
- Never modify an already-applied migration. Create a new migration to fix mistakes.

---

## Lombok Rules

Allowed:
- `@Getter`, `@Setter`
- `@Builder`
- `@RequiredArgsConstructor`
- `@Slf4j`
- `@NoArgsConstructor` (when JPA requires it — pair with `@Builder` using `@AllArgsConstructor`)

Avoid:
- `@Data` on entities — generates `equals`/`hashCode` using all fields, which breaks Hibernate lazy loading
- `@EqualsAndHashCode` on entities — define manually using only the `id` field

---

## File Uploads

- Maximum file size: **5 MB** per file.
- Allowed MIME types: `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `application/pdf`.
- Store the file path/URL in the database. Never store binary file content as a BLOB in the DB.
- Validate both file size and MIME type in the service layer before persisting.
- Use a dedicated upload service (`FileStorageService`) — never mix upload logic into domain service methods.

---

## CORS

- Define CORS in a `WebMvcConfigurer` bean in `config/`. Never use `@CrossOrigin` on controllers.
- Allowed origins must come from `application-{profile}.yml`. Never hardcode allowed origins.

---

## Environment & Profile Configuration

- Use `application.yml` for shared defaults.
- Use `application-dev.yml`, `application-staging.yml`, `application-prod.yml` for environment-specific overrides.
- Never hardcode secrets, passwords, or API keys. Use environment variables or a secrets manager.
- Never commit `application-prod.yml` with real credentials to version control.

---

## Security

- Spring Security filter chain must deny all requests by default (`anyRequest().authenticated()`).
- Public endpoints (login, registration, Swagger UI) must be explicitly listed in the security config.
- JWT validation filter placed before `UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter`.
- `@EnableMethodSecurity` required on the security config class.
- `@PreAuthorize` at the service method level is the second line of defense.
- `// TODO: Define RoleConstants before implementing @PreAuthorize — example roles: SUPER_ADMIN, TEMPLE_ADMIN, DEVOTEE, AUDITOR`

---

## Approval Workflow

- Staging tables must mirror the main table schema plus: `status VARCHAR(20)` (indexed), `submitted_at`, `reviewed_at`, `reviewed_by`, and a nullable FK to the main table.
- Enforce status transitions via a `validateTransition()` method in the service layer before every status update.
- `REJECTED` is immutable — throw `IllegalStateException` on any attempt to transition away from it.
- Only `APPROVED` staging records trigger a write to the main table.

---

## Optimistic Locking

- Use `@Version` on entities that are concurrently edited (staging records, main registrations).
- `OptimisticLockingFailureException` must be handled in the global exception handler.
